questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which three states formed the Triple Alliance when it was originally created?
options: Italy, France, and the United States
questions.explanation: The textbook identifies Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy as the original Triple Alliance members.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Gavrilo Princip as the Serbian nationalist who assassinated Franz Ferdinand.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Under the Schlieffen Plan, Germany proposed attacking France through which country?
questions.explanation: The Schlieffen Plan called for an attack on France through Belgium.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which battle halted the German advance in September 1914?
questions.explanation: The German advance was forced back at the Battle of the Marne in September 1914.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What type of German campaign helped lead the United States to enter World War I?
options: A campaign to form the League of Nations
questions.explanation: Germany’s unrestricted submarine campaign was one factor that led the United States to declare war.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which technology was used during World War I according to the textbook?
questions.explanation: The source lists poisonous gases among the technologies used in World War I.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which imperial dynasty collapsed in Russia after World War I?
questions.explanation: The textbook lists the Romanovs of Russia among the dynasties that collapsed after the war.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which political group was led by Lenin?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Lenin as leader of the Bolsheviks.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What form of rule ended when Tsar Nicholas II was deposed in February 1917?
questions.explanation: Nicholas II’s deposition ended the rule of the Romanov Dynasty.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What were the Soviets described as in the textbook?
questions.explanation: The textbook defines Soviets as councils or coordinating bodies.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Where was the League of Nations headquartered?
questions.explanation: The source says the League of Nations was headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which United States president proposed forming the League of Nations?
questions.explanation: The textbook states that President Woodrow Wilson proposed the League of Nations.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What event began the Great Depression according to the textbook?
options: The Wall Street stock market crash
questions.answer: The Wall Street stock market crash
questions.explanation: The source dates the beginning of the Great Depression to the Wall Street stock market crash of October 1929.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In which country was a Fascist state established in 1922?
questions.explanation: The textbook says a Fascist state was established in Italy in 1922.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which dispute did the League of Nations peacefully negotiate in 1926?
options: The Mosul dispute between Iraq and Turkey
questions.answer: The Mosul dispute between Iraq and Turkey
questions.explanation: The League negotiated a peaceful outcome to the Iraq–Turkey conflict over Mosul in 1926.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What did Mussolini do to Italy’s political parties as totalitarianism rose?
options: He dissolved all parties except his own
He transferred control to the League
He made foreign parties rule Italy
questions.answer: He dissolved all parties except his own
questions.explanation: The source says Mussolini dissolved all political parties except his own.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What was the name of Hitler’s autobiography written during imprisonment?
questions.explanation: The textbook says Hitler wrote Mein Kampf during imprisonment and it was published in 1926.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What policy did Britain and France follow by allowing some territorial seizures by Fascist states?
questions.explanation: Britain and France followed appeasement in an effort to avoid another world war.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: What did the Germans call their 1939 campaign in Poland?
questions.explanation: The Germans called their Polish campaign Blitzkrieg, meaning lightning war.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Which event brought the United States into the Second World War?
questions.explanation: After Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941, the United States declared war on Japan.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Growing rivalry and mistrust contributed to the formation of military alliances before World War I.
questions.explanation: The source says growing rivalries and mutual mistrust led to several military alliances among the Great Powers.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: The New Economic Policy restored smaller enterprises to their owners and allowed peasants to sell grain for profit.
questions.explanation: The NEP restored smaller enterprises, permitted grain sales for profit, and revived commerce.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: The United States became a member of the League of Nations after its formation.
questions.explanation: The U.S. Congress resisted membership, and the United States did not join the League.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: The United Nations Organization replaced the League of Nations after World War II.
questions.explanation: The source says the urge to maintain world peace gave birth to the UN, which replaced the League.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Name one root cause of World War I identified in the textbook.
questions.answer: Mutual defense alliances, imperialism, militarism, or nationalism.
questions.explanation: The textbook identifies these as major causes that set the stage for World War I.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: State one consequence of the Treaty of Versailles for Germany described in the textbook.
questions.answer: Germany faced military restrictions, was assigned responsibility for the war, had to pay reparations, or lost substantial territory.
questions.explanation: The source lists military restrictions, war responsibility, reparations, and territorial losses as effects on Germany.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Give one factor that weakened the Provisional Government in 1917.
questions.answer: It failed to end food shortages or bring the war to an end.
questions.explanation: The textbook says the Provisional Government lost public support because it did not resolve food shortages or end the war.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: State one principal goal of the League of Nations.
questions.answer: Preventing wars through collective security and disarmament, or settling disputes through negotiation and arbitration.
questions.explanation: The Covenant’s goals included collective security, disarmament, negotiation, and arbitration.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Give one effect of the Great Depression stated in the textbook.
questions.answer: Falling income, tax revenue, profits, prices, international trade, industrial output, or employment; high unemployment; bank failures; or falling crop prices.
questions.explanation: The source describes severe declines in trade, employment, income, prices, and banking stability.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Give one postwar condition in Italy that favoured the rise of Fascism.
questions.answer: Disappointment with the Treaty of Versailles, economic collapse, scarcity of natural resources, labour unrest, unemployment, or fear of communism.
questions.explanation: The source links Fascism’s rise to postwar disappointment and severe political, social, and economic problems.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: Name one major Allied power listed for World War II.
questions.answer: France, Britain, the United States, or the Soviet Union.
questions.explanation: The source identifies France, Britain, the USA, and the USSR as the main Allied Powers.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: State one major effect of World War II listed in the textbook.
questions.answer: Immense human and material loss, hastened decolonization, emergence of the USA and USSR as superpowers, the Cold War, or formation of the UNO.
questions.explanation: The textbook lists these as far-reaching effects of World War II.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did Austria-Hungary declare war on Serbia?
questions.explanation: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did the United States declare war on Germany?
questions.explanation: The United States declared war on Germany on 6 April 1917.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did the Bolsheviks sign the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk and formally withdraw Russia from World War I?
questions.explanation: The source says Russia formally withdrew after signing the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany in 1918.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year was the League of Nations founded?
questions.explanation: The League was founded on 10 January 1920 following the Paris Peace Conference.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did the Wall Street crash that began the Great Depression occur?
questions.explanation: The source dates the Wall Street stock market crash to October 1929.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did the Nazis come to power in Germany?
questions.explanation: The textbook says the Nazis came to power in Germany in 1933.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did Germany invade Poland, marking the beginning of World War II?
questions.explanation: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, marking the beginning of World War II.

questions.unitTitle: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
questions.question: In what year did Japan unconditionally surrender at the end of World War II?
questions.explanation: Japan unconditionally surrendered after the United States dropped atomic bombs in August 1945 and occupied Tokyo in September.
